sentences.text: Task 4 You are now attending a meeting of the research team with Linda and two other researchers called Simon and Sandy who are reporting on the survey results Based on what you hear in the conversation
between Linda and the researchers, fill in the spaces in the report below with details of the survey.
Physis and recommendations for improvements.
Remember to pay attention to spelling and grammar.
One space has been filled in for you as an example.
You now have one minute to study the task.
At the end of the task, you will have two minutes to tidy up your answers.
Alright, Chris, I’ve completed the framework of the report for you.
You just have to fill in the details and remember to pay attention to grammar and spelling when you're doing that.
Simon has counted all our responses and come up with some percentage figures along with Traveler's comments.
So, how did the Traveler's radar eating establishment, Simon?
Pretty well, actually.
About 60 % said they found the services impressive.
Well, it’s always good to impress people Then fifteen percent weren't happy with the range.
Fifty percent? No, fifteen.
And twenty five percent hadn't used any restaurants, so they couldn't say which ones they preferred.
Okay. Don’t bother writing about the fifteen percent, Chris.
We'll let people work that out for themselves.
Alright. Let’s move on to suggestions.
How do people think our food choices can be improved?
Well, first off, we should reduce the number of fast food outlets.
Less in the way of hamburgers, hot dogs, fried chicken and other salty snacks.
Yes, I have to agree, we do need to reduce them.
There's too much emphasis on fast food.
Go on. Another request was to increase medium -priced restaurants.
Either you have very cheap fast food outlets or up -market eateries that are too pricey.
Increasing medium -priced restaurants would help balance things out.
Fair enough. That’s worth noting down.
Finally, many felt we should provide a greater variety of food.
And what did they mean by greater variety?
Well Well, Different cuisines really.
Many wanted Japanese food.
There is some available but not really high quality stuff.
They were also a lot of requests for Indian food, and not just from Indians.
The Japanese and the Singaporeans love curry, and so do many westerners.
Any other requests?
Well, there were a few for Middle Eastern food, things like kebabs and falafels.
Middle Eastern food has a whole range of possibilities.
Interesting. Okay, let's move on to other facilities now.
What sort of requests did the traveller’s make?
Sandy? Well, several people felt there should be more places of worship.
Places of worship.
You mean like chapels, that sort of thing?
We already have one of those.
Yes, but we don’t have a Muslim prayer room, for example.
That's a bit of an oversight, really, isn’t it?
Write it down, Chris.
You can spell Muslim either M -U -S -L -I -M or M -O -S -L -E -M, Your choice.
Oh, and prayer is spelled P -R -A -Y -E -R.
Got that? But Any more places of worship to add, Sandy?
Well, I’m not sure of this count, but someone suggested a meditation room.
I like that idea.
meditation's a good thing to do before you get on a plane, and it’s not only Buddhists who like to do it.
It’s definitely worth including in the report.
There were also a number of requests for more entertainment facilities.
Such as? Well, I’m not sure if everyone would count this as an entertainment facility, but more than one person suggested a game centre.
I don’t think the Airport Authority would be keen to give space to a game centre, but I guess we ought to make a note of it.
Something they might be more happy to go for is an art gallery.
Many travellers said they'd seen them in other airports and thought it was a great idea.
Yes, I can see why.
There's something very relaxing about art galleries.
Okay, to sum up then, travellers at the airport felt that the facilities provided were mostly satisfactory.
I'd say that was about right, yes.
So let's increase someone's level of satisfaction even more.
Would you like to pull the name out of the lucky draw hat, Sandy?
Okay, Sure. Oh, it’s er, Mr Pot of Justaville, USA.
His first name's not Jack by any chance is it?
That's right. How did you know that?
